text.p: These are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Malta reports stronger early tourism bookings. British tour operators have reported more bookings than last year for summer holidays in Malta as the tourism industry picks up in Britain. British tourists account for nearly half of Malta's visitors. Tourism was down some seven percent in 1996.

- Depressed property market is good news for buyers. Sales of property have slumped as people await the presentation of the new government's first budget on Monday. The budget is excpected to include the removal of Value Added Tax.
- Economist Noel Zarb Adami named chairman of the state-owned communications agency Telemalta, replacing John Camilleri, appointed two years ago by the previous government.

- Maltese government invited for Moscow talks. The two countries enjoy good relations, but Russia owes Malta several million dollars for six timber carriers ordered by the former Soviet Union in the eighties. Four of the ships built by Malta Shipbuilding have not been delivered due to payment problems.

- Three environmentalists, members of a "Front against the Hilton", are camping outside the prime minister's office in Valletta on hunger strike, demanding an inquiry into the building of a new Hilton Hotel to replace an old one. The activists say the new $100 million complex will harm the marina.
